_source_verification_note: Every ats_sources entry below was reached live and its company identity confirmed on 2026-07-27, either from the Greenhouse board metadata `name` field or from the locations/departments on its own postings. Token guessing produces convincing impostors -- `greenhouse/archer` is Archer Veterinary Clinic, `greenhouse/apex` is Apex Eye, `greenhouse/axiom` is a consultancy in Atlanta and Belfast, `ashby/sierra` is Sierra AI, and `ashby/icon` is an unrelated startup -- so confirm identity, not just that the endpoint returns JSON, before adding an employer here. The 43 entries appended on 2026-09-20 were found by resolving the apply links on earlycareerradar.com back to their underlying ATS boards, then confirming each one independently: every endpoint was called live at the same URL pipeline.py builds, and company identity was read out of the posting text rather than trusted from the token. That mattered -- `workday/aksteel` is Cleveland-Cliffs, `workday/flir` is Teledyne, and `workday/cat` reaches Caterpillar filtered to its Solar Turbines site. The aggregator itself was not added as a source: it carried deadlines on 2 of 4,911 roles and left work authorization unstated on 74% of them.

agent_discovery.note: Channels an agent session reaches through Agent Reach, then imports with `import-discovered`. pipeline.py never calls these itself -- it stays stdlib-only and offline-testable. Verified reachable 2026-07-26.

linkedin.note: Returns mixed kinds and badge-suffixed titles; import-discovered normalizes both. Relevance is loose -- keep discovery_title_terms filtering on. Keywords and locations are per student: set them in config/sources.local.json.

exa.note: Best for surfacing employers not yet in ats_sources. rejected_sources.note: Probed on 2026-07-27 and deliberately not adopted. Recorded so the same ground is not re-covered every few months.
rejected_sources.themuse: Keyless public API at https://www.themuse.com/api/public/jobs. Its whole 'Science and Engineering' category holds only 117 internships nationally, dominated by one retailer's Arkansas postings and by roles in China, Italy, and Singapore, and it still serves stale 2025 listings. Its `location` filter also leaks -- a query for Austin returned New York and Quebec roles. Not worth the request budget as a default source.
rejected_sources.workable_recruitee_rippling_bamboohr: All four have clean public JSON endpoints and adapters would be easy, but a sweep across ~70 mechanical/hardware employers found essentially no real boards on them -- the few hits were generic-token false positives. Adding the adapters would be dead code until a specific employer is found using one.
rejected_sources.careerjet: Public API endpoint refused the connection on probe.
rejected_sources.nsf_etap: etap.nsf.gov reset the connection on probe. NSF REU stays a manual_check_sources entry.
rejected_sources.remotive_arbeitnow_himalayas: Remote-work aggregators, keyless, but software-skewed and Europe-heavy. Near-zero mechanical intern yield.
rejected_sources.jooble_jsearch: Both live and both need keys. Not adopted only because Adzuna already covers the US aggregator slot with a better location filter -- revisit if Adzuna's free tier proves too thin.
rejected_sources.nasa_on_usajobs: NASA internships are not on USAJOBS -- 0 student-path NASA postings there against 14 NASA postings total, verified 2026-07-26. intern.nasa.gov is the real channel and stays a manual_check_sources entry.
rejected_sources.enterprise_ats_icims_teamtailor_jobvite: Probed on 2026-08-05 across 59 mechanical/aerospace/manufacturing/energy employers absent from this file (Lockheed, RTX, Blue Origin, Tesla, Caterpillar, John Deere, Emerson, Boston Scientific, Halliburton, and similar). Only 5 of 59 resolved to any board -- icims:generaldynamics, icims:parker, icims:commonwealth, icims:boston, teamtailor:firefly -- and every one returned 0 postings matching discovery_title_terms. The boards that did resolve carried 1-20 postings, far too few to be a real corporate board for those employers, so most are the generic-token false positives this file already warns about (`icims:boston` is not Boston Scientific). The root cause is structural: unlike Greenhouse and Ashby, these vendors' tenants are not derivable from a company name -- iCIMS uses careers-<tenant>, and Phenom/SuccessFactors/Radancy/OracleCloud/Avature/Cornerstone sit behind branded hosts with no guessable pattern at all. Adapters would be dead code until specific employer tenants are identified by hand. Revisit only with a concrete employer and its real careers URL, not with a vendor.
rejected_sources.outreach_slug_impostors_2026_09_20: Slug guesses from outreach company names that resolved to a live board belonging to someone else. Recorded so a later discover-ats run is not adopted on trust. greenhouse/impact is impact.com, an affiliate-marketing platform, not IMPACT Drones. greenhouse/paradigm is Paradigm, a workplace-culture consultancy, not Paradigm Robotics. greenhouse/bravo is BRAVO - A Cooperative Company, an MEP and fire-protection firm, not Bravo Ordnance. ashby/orbital is a real-estate legal-AI company with no mention of Orbital Arc anywhere on the board. All four came from the bare-first-word slug candidate, which is exactly the case slug_candidates warns about.
